cases.why: the headline figure -- how far apart the two blues were in prose -- goes stale by one digit. This is the PR #52 defect exactly: a real-looking number in a permanent source comment, wrong in the code for as long as it takes someone to re-run the method by hand. Nothing behaves differently, so only an executable assertion can catch it.

the comparison number goes stale. It is the one that makes the defect legible -- the charts drew the same two models far apart while the prose drew them close -- so a wrong value here quietly weakens the argument for the whole change.
cases.find: charts drew the same pair 49.3 apart
cases.replace: charts drew the same pair 44.3 apart

cases.why: the residual pair is the honest part of the comment: --accent and --series-a stay close, and it is tolerable only because they never share a view. Whoever checks that claim later reads these three numbers. The light-theme CVD figure is the last of the three and the easiest to leave behind, which is the same position the 'seven pairs' sentence occupied on PR #52 when it got away.
